review.tagline: Python library for composable autodiff, JIT and vectorization of NumPy-style code
review.summary: JAX is a Python array library that transforms NumPy-style functions with grad (forward and reverse-mode autodiff), jit (XLA compilation) and vmap (auto-vectorization). The transformations compose, and code runs on CPU, NVIDIA GPU, Google TPU and AMD GPU, with experimental Apple and Intel GPU support. Scaling across devices uses automatic, explicit or manual (shard_map) sharding.
review.audience: ML researchers and engineers writing numerical or model code for accelerators
strengths: grad, jit and vmap compose arbitrarily, including higher-order derivatives and per-example gradients
Differentiates through Python loops, branches, recursion and closures
Three sharding modes (auto, explicit, manual) for scaling across many devices
Compiles via XLA to CPU, NVIDIA, TPU and AMD targets using pip extras
weaknesses: README calls it a research project with sharp edges; not an official Google product
jit restricts the Python control flow a function can use
No native Windows GPU support; WSL2 GPU is experimental
Apple and Intel GPU backends are experimental
